explanations.answer: To be tempted by the devil
explanations.explanation: That's exactly what the verse says: Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness "…to be tempted by the devil." (Matthew 4:1) Notice who does the leading. It's the Spirit, not a wrong turn on the map. Some trips start with a plan, and this one did.

Good guess, since a quiet place feels like a prayer spot. But Matthew 4:1 gives a different reason: Jesus was led "…to be tempted by the devil." Nothing in this passage says anything about choosing disciples. I'd keep that one in the dough bin for another day.

King Herod shows up earlier in Matthew's Gospel (Matthew 2:1), but not here. The text says the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness "…to be tempted by the devil." (Matthew 4:1) So this isn't a hiding trip. Jesus goes out there led by the Spirit.

Bread it is. The tempter says, "If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread." (Matthew 4:3) Jesus had fasted forty days and forty nights, so I think a loaf looked pretty good right about then. Friend, I'd have been tempted too.

Water makes sense for a dry wilderness, but that's not what the tempter says. His words are, "…tell these stones to become bread." (Matthew 4:3) The verse before it says Jesus was hungry after fasting. So the test points at His empty stomach.

Gold sounds fancy, and the devil does bring up riches later on. But here the tempter says, "…tell these stones to become bread." (Matthew 4:3) The moment is about hunger, since Jesus had been fasting forty days and forty nights. Gold would've been a very shiny way to miss a meal.

Not quite. Jesus doesn't turn the stones into anything. Instead He answers, "Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God." (Matthew 4:4) He's hungry, and He still doesn't take the tempter's dare.

Right, no stone-to-bread trick happens. The tempter says to do it, and Jesus answers, "Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God." (Matthew 4:4) He's hungry, and He still doesn't do it. He answers with Scripture and leaves the stones as stones.
Yep. The devil says, "throw Yourself down." (Matthew 4:6) He's standing Jesus on the pinnacle of the temple when he says it. Friend, up that high I'd be hugging the roof with my whole mustache.

Fire from heaven is a big dramatic moment in other Bible stories, like 1 Kings 18:38, but not in this one. On the pinnacle of the temple, the devil says, "throw Yourself down." (Matthew 4:6) That's the dare. It's about jumping, not about fire.

explanations.answer: Make the crowds bow to Him
explanations.explanation: No crowds show up in this scene at all. The devil's dare on the temple is, "throw Yourself down." (Matthew 4:6) Bowing comes later, on the mountain, and there the devil wants Jesus to bow to him. Different test, different spot.

That's right. Jesus replies, "It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’…" (Matthew 4:7) The devil said "It is written…" first, and Jesus answers with Scripture too. Jesus points to another line instead of taking the jump.

This one is true, so let me set it straight. Jesus says, "It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’…" (Matthew 4:7) He doesn't jump, and He doesn't argue. He simply answers with another line of Scripture.

explanations.answer: To fall down and worship him
explanations.explanation: That's the price tag. The devil says, "All this I will give You, if You will fall down and worship me." (Matthew 4:9) He's showing off all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. Friend, that's a big offer with a very big catch.
The devil never asks for silence. His words are, "All this I will give You, if You will fall down and worship me." (Matthew 4:9) He wants worship. That's the whole deal.

explanations.answer: To leave the land of Israel
explanations.explanation: The devil doesn't mention Israel's borders at all. What he asks is, "if You will fall down and worship me." (Matthew 4:9) In return, he offers all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. So the ask is worship, not a move.
Yes! Jesus says, "Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only." (Matthew 4:10) Before that He tells the devil, "Away from Me, Satan!" Notice the word "only." It leaves no room for anyone else.
No king gets named here. Jesus says, "Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only." (Matthew 4:10) The worship goes to the Lord God and nobody else. A crown doesn't change that.

The prophets don't come up in this scene. Jesus says, "Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only." (Matthew 4:10) The worship goes to the Lord your God. That word "only" leaves no room for anyone else.

That's it. The text says, "Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him." (Matthew 4:11) Right after Jesus says, "Away from Me, Satan!" the devil leaves. Then angels come and minister to Jesus. The three tests are done.
The text counts three tests, then stops. Matthew 4:11 says, "Then the devil left Him…" No fourth round shows up. After the devil leaves, angels come and minister to Jesus.

No begging in this scene. Matthew 4:11 just says, "Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him." He leaves right after Jesus tells him, "Away from Me, Satan!" It's quiet, and it's over.
